newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU 1998 budgets will be weighed for EMU - de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EU 1998 budgets will be weighed for EMU - de Silguy.

text.p: The European Commission will look at member states' 1998 budgets alongside 1997 economic data in deciding who meets the criteria for European currency union, Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said.

De Silguy, the EU's commissioner for monetary affairs, said the budgets would help show which countries could sustain the strict borrowing and inflation limits for joining a single currency under Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"The Commission will take into account the real figures for 1997 but also, and importantly, the budgets for 1998," de Silguy said at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
De Silguy said the criteria laid down by the Maastricht Treaty would be "strictly interpreted" when the Commission in early 1998 weighs who can join the currency with the launch of the Euro in 1999.

The Euro would be credible and stable because of a stability pact aimed at keeping member countries on a stringent fiscal path after 1999 and because of the independence of the new European Central Bank, de Silguy said.
"The independence of the European Central Bank is a point that is not open to renegotiation," he added.
De Silguy also said he expected new investment to boost European growth, which would help EU countries meet the EMU criteria.
"My personal forecast is that once investors realise that (European) interest rates really are very low, investment will pick up and growth will be faster than forecast," he said.
